## Management

• Microsoft Intune and other MDM solutions define and manage agent containment, configuration and compliance policy.

• Microsoft Entra governs identity, authentication, and access.

• Agent 365, Microsoft Defender, and Microsoft Purview extend observability, security, and management into agent activity workflows.

## Why identity is foundational

## Where Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) fits in an enterprise agent-security strategy

• Identity and access with Microsoft Entra Agent ID: Agent identity helps distinguish agent activity from a user’s own activity so organizations can apply appropriate access, security, and governance controls. Microsoft Entra Agent ID provides the identity foundation for supported agent scenarios, including identifying agent activity and enabling access controls as agents interact with cloud resources. On Windows, local security boundaries can further isolate an agent’s processes and resource access from the user. Together, these capabilities help organizations distinguish and govern agent activity across local and cloud interactions, with support varying by agent and scenario.

• Local agent containment with Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC): MXC is the policy-driven containment layer. Agents who adopt it run supported execution inside an OS-enforced boundary. MXC applies runtime controls over what the agent can read/write (for example, local files), which resources it can call, and what requests or results can flow to permitted endpoints and MCP servers.

• Securing AI on the endpoint with Microsoft Intune: Intune delivers MXC containment policy for managed Windows devices, so agent workloads run within enterprise-defined boundaries. Intune also governs agent access to company resources through device compliance, protects work data with app protection policies for supported agents, restricts unauthorized agents, and applies policy to enable Microsoft Defender runtime protection.

• Local-agent discovery, runtime protection, and investigation with Microsoft Defender : Microsoft Defender discovers supported local agents and provides endpoint context, including associated users, devices, processes, and configured MCP connections. Runtime protection helps detect and block malicious instructions and tool interactions in supported agent workflows, while alerts and investigation capabilities help security teams understand and respond to threats.

• Data loss prevention for local agents with Microsoft Purview: Microsoft Purview extends data loss prevention policies to supported local-agent interactions, including prompts and tool calls, helping organizations detect and block inappropriate sharing of sensitive information. This enables organizations to apply data protection policies as agents work with enterprise information.

• Bring local AI agents under management with Microsoft Agent 365: As organizations adopt local AI agents, they need a consistent way to understand where agents are operating, what they can access, and which ones are authorized. Microsoft Agent 365 brings supported local agents and their MCP connections into a unified Agent registry, giving administrators visibility into their AI estate and the tools agents use. With Dynamic Agent Risk, agent templates, and integrated Microsoft security controls, organizations can prioritize risks, apply governance policies at scale, bring approved agents under management, and restrict unauthorized agents.

## Prepare before you deploy

• Business objective: the user outcome and why agent access is required.

• Execution model: how work is performed across process flows, tools, commands, files, and endpoints.

• Control boundaries: where identity context, data sensitivity, network exposure, or administrative privilege changes require controls.

• Operating readiness: required OS and agent versions, management settings, security policies, deployment groups, support readiness, and rollout governance.

## Roll out Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) progressively

## 1. Observe Before Enforce (Policy Evidence Phase)

• Enforcement : ungranted access is blocked; no activity report. Use when running production policy.

• Learning - enforced + recorded : ungranted access is blocked and recorded in an activity report. Use to diagnose containment failures and confirm only required access is granted.

• Permissive - allowed + recorded : access that policy would deny is allowed but recorded. Use in controlled pilots to observe behavior without interrupting users.

## 2. Develop the minimum policy that supports the workload

## 3. Validate in deployment rings

• Ring 0 — technical validation: limited number of users operated by the deployment team; prove assignment, version checks, telemetry, exclusion, and rollback.

• Ring 1 — informed early adopters: limited number of users close to the workload; validate real tasks and support documentation.

• Ring 2 — limited production: increased scale of users across representative device and network conditions.

• Ring 3 — broad deployment: expand only after success criteria and support capacity are met.

## 4. Match enforcement to confidence

## 5. Preserve an opt-out and rollback path

• الهوية: Microsoft Entra Agent ID يميّز نشاط الوكيل عن المستخدم.
• الاحتواء: Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) طبقة عزل تحدد ما يقرؤه الوكيل ويكتبه وما يستدعيه.
• الإدارة: Intune لسياسات الاحتواء، وDefender لاكتشاف الوكلاء المحليين وحمايتهم، وPurview وAgent 365 للمراقبة.

تساعد هذه الطبقات المؤسسات على الاستفادة من الوكلاء مع تقليل المخاطر.
